name: Corn Dolly

attributes.attribute: built from the last sheaf at harvest

sources: Meaden, George Terrence. The Goddess of the Stones: The Language of the Megaliths. London: Souvenir Press, 1991, 204-205.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The Corn Dolly, also called the Corn Maiden, is a symbol of Scottish and Irish folklore. People shaped it from straw at harvest time, often from the last sheaf cut. Its origins are obscure but are mythic or ritual. It is linked to two figures of arguable age: the CAILLEACH or hag, and BRIGIT or the Bride, who may be the hag maiden form. People stored the Dolly in a house or barn from autumn to spring, when it took part in sowing and rites of new life.

okr.objective: The Corn Dolly is a harvest symbol of folklore.
key_results: It was shaped from straw at harvest.
It used the last sheaf of the field.
It links the Cailleach and the Bride.
It was kept from autumn to spring.
